name: NC-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+24 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic House seats in the country
Incumbent Alma Adams holds an overwhelming cash advantage ($484K on hand vs. $3.8K for Codiga)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
No general-election polling or expert ratings; forecast rests on district fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's D+24 lean, Adams' incumbency, and her lopsided fundraising edge leave the Republican challenger with almost no visible path, and markets price a Democratic hold near 96 percent. With no polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals that all point in the same direction.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Adams or an unprecedented national shift toward Republicans could tighten the race, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 12th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 24 points. Alma Adams, the incumbent, is running for re-election and enters the fall with a decisive financial advantage: about $484,000 in the bank, compared with roughly $3,800 for Republican challenger Jack Codiga. No outside groups have spent in the race, and no general-election polls are available.

Prediction markets give Adams roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and the district's fundamentals point the same way. A margin in the mid-20s is the central expectation, with somewhat wider uncertainty because direct polling is absent. Barring an extraordinary development, the seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands.
